_about: NbS component catalogue. One entry per component type / guideline chapter. 'swmm' names the SWMM representation used by the .inp builder. Add new chapters here (with their rules in guidelines.json).

rain_garden.label: Rain garden
rain_garden.description: Shallow planted depression with engineered media; receives runoff from nearby paths, roofs and courts.

bioswale.label: Bioswale
bioswale.description: Vegetated channel along concentrated flow lines that conveys and infiltrates.

detention_pond.label: Detention pond
detention_pond.description: Dry basin at low points; stores storm water and releases it slowly through a controlled outlet.

retention_pond.label: Retention pond
retention_pond.description: Permanent pool with live storage above it and an overflow weir.

recharge_well.label: Recharge well
recharge_well.description: Shaft that passes pre-treated overflow to permeable strata below poor surface soils.

constructed_wetland.label: Constructed wetland
constructed_wetland.description: Multi-cell surface-flow wetland (forebay ~20 %, deepwater inlet ~10 %, shallow vegetated zone ~70 %) with adjustable outlet weir.
constructed_wetland.modelling_note: Hydrology: one storage node whose stage-area curve combines the zones; permanent pool = shallow zone depth; seepage only if unlined. Pollutant removal is not modelled by SWMM in this version.

edge_engineering.label: Edge engineering
edge_engineering.description: Soft, vegetated land-water edge (coir logs, live fascines, gabions) along drains and lake edges, with curb-cut inflow.
edge_engineering.modelling_note: Hydrology: vegetated swale LID along the edge (conveyance + infiltration). Bank stabilisation and habitat benefits are reported qualitatively only.

inline_check_dam.label: In-line SWD treatment (check dam)
inline_check_dam.description: Low gabion check dam (0.3-0.6 m) or baffle inside a storm water drain, creating a pool upstream with overflow notch; usually paired with separators, NSBBs or floating wetlands.
inline_check_dam.modelling_note: Hydrology: small storage pool behind the dam with a notch weir. Separators, NSBBs and floating wetlands treat water quality and are not credited with volume reduction.

green_bridge.label: Green bridge (check dam across a swale)
green_bridge.description: A low earth or stone crossing drawn across a bioswale: it holds water in the swale behind it up to its crest, and above the crest water spills over it into the next stretch. People walk across it.
green_bridge.modelling_note: Ground: the swale is raised to the crest under the bridge, so the flow map and the 2D storm pond behind it. SWMM: the pool behind each bridge is a storage node (a wedge whose area grows with depth to the pool area at the crest) with an overflow weir as long as the swale's bottom is wide; the swale's outflow passes through its bridges from upstream to downstream.
